title: a new ESLint finding on a JS file the branch touches

explain.what: ESLint found something new in a JS file the branch touches; the finding names the ESLint rule (LJ/<rule>).
explain.why: A linter knows the language better than a regex. Only what the branch adds counts, and the levels below say what holds a merge.
explain.fix: Fix what the message says. The rule's page on eslint.org explains it; a finding that must stay needs a waiver for LJ/<rule>.

no-unused-vars.what: A variable, import or parameter the branch adds is never used (ESLint no-unused-vars).
no-unused-vars.why: Unused code makes the reader look for a purpose that is not there. It is often the sign of an unfinished change or a left-over.
no-unused-vars.fix: Delete it. If it must stay unused (a required parameter), start its name with an underscore: _x.

no-duplicate-imports.what: A file imports from the same module in two import lines.
no-duplicate-imports.why: Two imports of one module make it harder to see what the file uses, and they often mean a merge or an edit went wrong.
no-duplicate-imports.fix: Merge them into one import line.

no-console.what: A debug left-over is in the code: console.log, console.debug, console.trace, console.dir or debugger.
no-console.why: Debug output clutters what the user sees and can leak data. A debugger statement stops the program when dev tools are open.
no-console.fix: Delete it. If the output is wanted, use the module's logger or print from a CLI module under engine/bin.

no-debugger.what: A debug left-over is in the code: console.log, console.debug, console.trace, console.dir or debugger.
no-debugger.why: Debug output clutters what the user sees and can leak data. A debugger statement stops the program when dev tools are open.
no-debugger.fix: Delete it. If the output is wanted, use the module's logger or print from a CLI module under engine/bin.

no-warning-comments.what: A new comment has a TODO, FIXME, HACK or XXX marker.
no-warning-comments.why: A marker in the code is a task that no list tracks. It stays in the code long after anyone remembers it.
no-warning-comments.fix: Do the work now, or record it (`norn road add` or a record) and delete the marker.

no-restricted-properties.why: With .only, the test runner runs that one test and silently skips the rest. The suite reports green while most tests did not run. A skipped test checks nothing, but the suite still looks green. Nobody notices when the code it covered breaks.
no-restricted-properties.fix: Fix the test, or delete it if it no longer applies. If it must skip on some machines, make skip a condition (for example the platform).

parse.what: A JS file the branch touches does not parse: ESLint read none of it.
parse.why: A file that does not parse checks nothing and fails at run time; no other lint finding can be trusted for it.
parse.fix: Fix the syntax error the message names (its line and column), then run the check again.

config-changed.what: The branch edits the lint config (eslint.config.mjs); the check keeps linting with the merge base's.
config-changed.why: Weakening the config is the cheapest way to clear a finding, and the config is code the gate runs.
config-changed.fix: Keep the config as it is, or ask the owner: his waiver for LJ/config-changed approves the rule change.
